question.worked_solution:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}\frac{x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}}{\sqrt{x}-yz} & =\frac{9-({1}^{2})({3}^{2})}{\sqrt{9}-1(3)} \\  & =\frac{9-9}{3-3} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we can simplify the limit by first multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}\frac{x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}}{\sqrt{x}-yz} & ={lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}\frac{(x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2})(\sqrt{x}+yz)}{(\sqrt{x}-yz)(\sqrt{x}+yz)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}\frac{(x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2})(\sqrt{x}+yz)}{x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}\frac{\cancel{(x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2})}(\sqrt{x}+yz)}{\cancel{x-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}(\sqrt{x}+yz)\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (9,1,3)}(\sqrt{x}+yz) & =\sqrt{9}+1(3) \\  & =3+3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $6.$
